chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a free man who had a female slave under his ownership, and he divorced her with a final divorce, then he bought her back; is it permissible for him to have sexual relations with her? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.يَطَأَهَا: To have sexual relations with her

ai.seo_question: Does a master need a new marriage contract if he divorces his female slave and buys her back?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a final divorce (talaq ba'in) severs the marital bond completely, meaning that merely repurchasing the slave woman does not automatically reinstate the previous marriage contract. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of female slaves (ummat al-ayd) in Shia jurisprudence, where the mechanism of remarriage differs from that of free women, requiring explicit re-agreement or new contract formation rather than automatic reinstatement upon purchase.
